Āṇḍapillai
a Tamil alias of Tālavṛntanivāsin.
--C. Prayogavṛtti on Āpastambasūtra.
--C. on Āśval. śr. sūtra etc.,

.
--Prayogas relating to all the three Vedas. R. A. Sastri II. p. 188.
This name is found in a variety of ways in North Indian catalogues,
--Aṇḍvila, Āḍabila, Anvilā, Āṇḍabilā,
--an. sometimes even texts or parts thereof, of Tālavṛntanivāsin are given in this name--Āṇḍ. prayoga, ºpaddhati an. so on or simply a. Āṇḍabilā, Uttarāṇḍapillai an. so on. Āṇḍapillai is a South Indian [Page043-a. Tamil name an. occurs in Col. inscriptions. For a. Sanskrit writer Āṇḍapillai Bhaṭṭa an. his Sanskrit verse in a. inscription of the time of Kulottuṅga Col. I, see
, para 13. His. personal name cannot be stated for certain; two mss. (
) mention it a. Keśava in a col.-like anuṣṭubh verse a. end, but in all other mss., a. this place, ‘Somapa’, a mere descriptive epithet, is read; one ms. (
) reads here ‘Kauśika’, instead of Keśava or Somapa. The following four entries are of mss. of his works the exact identities of which cannot be determined.

Āṇḍālūdeśika
ancestor of the a. of the Anaṅgamaṅgalabhāṇa (ANDAldezikavaMzajaH kavirayam etc.). See K. M. edn.
